findings.evidence: "The benefits team tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Assign stipend-budget tracking to a single named owner and remove the duplicate, conflicting statements from the other two sections.
findings.violation: This exact responsibility is repeated later under "Special Cases" ("The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget...") and "Questions and Updates" ("The people operations office tracks the stipend budget...") with three different owners named for the same task, contradicting each other.

findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Specify the document being referenced (e.g., "a printed copy of the current stipend budget summary").
findings.violation: It is unclear what document "a printed copy" refers to - the antecedent (the stipend budget, a non-physical tracking activity) doesn't naturally have a "printed copy" employees would request.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Define the "stipend clock" concept (e.g., the 90-day service requirement or the benefit-year claim window) before referencing it.
findings.violation: "The stipend clock" is used without ever being introduced or defined earlier in the policy, so the reader cannot tell what is being measured or when it started.

findings.evidence: "eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details"
findings.fix: Use one consistent name for the stipend throughout the document, or explicitly define "workspace stipend" as a distinct benefit if that is intended.
findings.violation: The document defines only a "home-office equipment stipend" (see Eligibility's opening sentence); "workspace stipend" is a different, undefined term and it's unclear whether it names the same benefit or a separate one.

findings.evidence: "The workspace must sit inside the employee's primary residence for the stipend to apply. A workspace located in a shared coworking space does not qualify... A workspace used only occasionally for calls does not meet the bar... The reviewer confirms the workspace address matches... A workspace shared with a roommate can still qualify... A workspace that changes address... needs a fresh confirmation... A workspace confirmation from more than one year ago no longer satisfies..."
findings.fix: Convert this paragraph into a bulleted checklist of discrete workspace-eligibility criteria.
findings.violation: Nine distinct eligibility rules are buried in one dense run-on paragraph of similarly-structured sentences, making the criteria hard to scan, verify, or audit against a specific case.

findings.evidence: "A workspace confirmation from more than one year ago no longer satisfies the stipend requirement on its own."
findings.fix: Either state what else (if anything) can supplement an old confirmation, or remove "on its own" if no such exception exists.
findings.location: Eligibility, last sentence of workspace paragraph
findings.violation: "On its own" implies there is some additional factor that could make an old confirmation sufficient, but no such factor is ever described, leaving the rule incomplete.

findings.evidence: "Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins."
findings.fix: Reconcile the two sections into one consistent list of required documents (receipt vs. photo of receipt, and whether a purchase order/approval form is mandatory).
findings.violation: This contradicts "Required Documentation," which states "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests" and never mentions a required purchase order or approval form at all.

findings.evidence: "Employees must submit the receipt... before the review begins... Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request."
findings.fix: Lay out the application steps in a single ordered list so the actual sequence (draft, review summary, final submission, manager review) is unambiguous.
findings.violation: The sequence is contradictory: documents are submitted "before the review begins," but then the employee reviews a summary "before submitting the final request," implying two different submission events without clarifying which is authoritative or how they relate.

findings.evidence: "The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: State explicitly what event starts the three-day countdown.
findings.violation: "After three days" doesn't specify the starting point (submission date, start of the pause, or the two-business-day review deadline), so the actual timing is ambiguous.

findings.evidence: "an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives"
findings.fix: Replace "item" with a specific term such as "missing document" or "missing information."
findings.violation: "Item" is ambiguous here - it could mean a missing document/piece of information or a missing piece of equipment, especially since "equipment category" and "equipment item" are used elsewhere in the same section.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: List the specific request types or amounts that require more than a photo of the receipt.
findings.violation: The exceptions implied by "most requests" are never identified, so employees cannot know when a photo is insufficient.

findings.evidence: "Additionally, employees shall retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Employees must retain receipts for one year after the purchase date" to match the document's style.
findings.violation: The sudden use of "shall" breaks from the plain, direct phrasing used everywhere else in the document (e.g., "Employees must submit..."), creating an inconsistent register.

findings.evidence: "The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount."
findings.fix: Add the actual stipend amount(s) or reimbursement cap per equipment category.
findings.violation: A section titled "Reimbursement Amounts" never actually states any stipend amount, cap, or percentage covered - the core information promised by the heading is missing.

findings.evidence: "this office may ask for a brief photo check once a year"
findings.fix: Name the specific office responsible for the annual photo check.
findings.violation: "This office" has no clear antecedent - the preceding sentence names no office, and the document elsewhere names several different offices (benefits team, finance office, people operations, finance liaison), so it's unclear who conducts the photo check.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk... while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category."
findings.fix: Split this into separate sentences stating the general one-device rule and the second-device exception as a distinct, clearly flagged carve-out, and reconcile it with the one-claim-per-year rule in Eligibility.
findings.violation: This single, extremely long run-on sentence is difficult to parse and internally contradicts itself (asserting "one device per category" while simultaneously describing conditions for allowing a "second device"), and it also conflicts with Eligibility's statement that "the stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year."

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Either add an actual glossary of terms under this heading, or rename the section to match its process content, define "stipend item," and convert "you" to third person for consistency.
findings.violation: The heading promises definitions of terms, but the section instead describes a process, introduces the undefined term "stipend item" (not used or defined anywhere else), and switches to second-person voice ("you") inconsistent with the third-person voice used in every other section.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Remove the erroneous comma and align this section's steps with the full process described in "How to Apply," or merge the two sections.
findings.violation: The comma before "and" incorrectly joins only two list items as if part of a longer series, and the two steps listed are far less complete than the multi-step process already described in "How to Apply" (receipt, approval form, purchase order, confirmation summary, final submission), creating an inconsistent process description.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicated text and replace it with actual special-case scenarios, or delete the section.
findings.violation: This is a near-verbatim duplicate of the Program Overview text (with the owner changed from "benefits team" to "finance liaison"), and the section does not describe any actual special case despite its heading.

findings.evidence: "The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department."
findings.fix: Clarify that the approver is determined by the employee's department and confirm whether this is always the direct manager.
findings.violation: It's unclear whose department is meant (the employee's) and this "correct approver" concept is never reconciled with Approval Timeline's statement that "the manager reviews the request," leaving it ambiguous whether the manager is always the approver.

findings.evidence: "The determination of stipend eligibility happens before any payment goes out. The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Rewrite in active voice naming the responsible party, and define what qualifies as a "repeat request."
findings.violation: A section titled "Review Responsibility" never names who is responsible for either determination or escalation (both sentences use passive/nominalized phrasing that hides the actor), and "repeat requests" is an undefined term not used anywhere else.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicated/conflated text, and add actual content about how employees can ask questions or receive policy updates.
findings.violation: This conflates two originally distinct statements from Program Overview - the "date stamp" sentence there described equipment catalog entries, not the stipend budget - producing a non-sequitur, and it's the third differently-attributed duplicate of the budget-tracking claim; the section also fails to address its own heading (how to ask questions or where updates are announced).
